doc.title: Manny Albam interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998

chapter: The Blues Is Everybody's Business and West Side Story
title: Choosing soloists: Nick Travis, Art Farmer, Cohn, Woods, Costa, and Mingus declining
summary: He chose the soloists in advance; Mingus declined and Vinny Burke, suggested by Eddie Costa, played bass.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Well the musical description that you’ve written was very specific. Was it written — did you have this whole scenario in mind when you started, even down to describing the muted sound of Nick Travis — I believe that’s the trumpet player’s name?

Yeah. Well both he and Art played in the mutes, there were two different mutes and each one traded off as a matter of fact. But oh yeah, I had all that, I knew who I was going to have. I knew I was going to have Nick, and I mentioned them. Nick, Art, Brookmeyer was going to be a soloist, Al Cohn was and Phil Woods and Gene Quill, who were the two great alto players. They were alter-egos for each other. And so I knew they would be there. Eddie Costa, an incredible piano player — unfortunately he ended his life too quickly in an automobile accident. But a marvelous player and so I knew he was going to be there. I figured Gene Orloff was going to be the concertmaster and I didn’t think violin solo until I came upon it. A lot of it is predetermined by just the people. Now I had gone after Charles Mingus as a bass soloist. Milt was on this and finally Vinny Burke was the soloist. Mingus said, “yeah let me think about it” and by the time he thought about it we’d already hired the rest of the band and he said no he didn’t want to do it. And so we scrounged around, and as a matter of fact Eddie Costa suggested Vinny Burke. They had been working as a duo for a while. And that’s the way all this came about. The thematic stuff for me is very simple stuff.
Well I’m glad you mention that, I just wanted to —
